\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{अंदेशा} (andeśā)}{अंदेशा (andeśā)}]{\hi{अंदेशा} (andeśā) — a worry; a misgiving}

\label{lesson:HI-C557-andesa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a groundless fear, then the Hindi for a firm decision.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अंदेशा}}
\textbf{\hi{अंदेशा}} — \emph{andeśā} — \textquotedblleft{}a worry; a misgiving\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{मुझे} \hi{अंदेशा} \hi{था} \hi{कि} \hi{ट्रेन} \hi{देर} \hi{से} \hi{आएगी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mujhe andeśā thā ki ṭren der se āegī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I had a feeling that the train would be late.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{अंदेशा}} (\emph{andeśā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{andēsha}, \textquotedblleft{}thought, anxiety\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{andeśā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{andeśā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Mujhe andeśā thā ki ṭren der se āegī.} — I had a feeling that the train would be late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a groundless fear, then the Hindi for a firm decision, then say \emph{andeśā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{अंदेशा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A worry; a misgiving\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{इत्मीनान} (itmīnān)}{इत्मीनान (itmīnān)}]{\hi{इत्मीनान} (itmīnān) — peace of mind, ease}

\label{lesson:HI-C557-itminan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a firm decision, then the Hindi for a worry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{इत्मीनान}}
\textbf{\hi{इत्मीनान}} — \emph{itmīnān} — \textquotedblleft{}peace of mind, ease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{सब} \hi{काम} \hi{पूरा} \hi{करके} \hi{मैं} \hi{इत्मीनान} \hi{से} \hi{सोया।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sab kām pūrā karke maiṁ itmīnān se soyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
With all the work finished I slept with my mind at rest.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{इत्मीनान}} (\emph{itmīnān}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{iṭmiʾnān}, \textquotedblleft{}tranquillity\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{itmīnān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{itmīnān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Sab kām pūrā karke maiṁ itmīnān se soyā.} — With all the work finished I slept with my mind at rest.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a firm decision, then the Hindi for a worry, then say \emph{itmīnān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{गारंटी} (gāraṇṭī)}{गारंटी (gāraṇṭī)}]{\hi{गारंटी} (gāraṇṭī) — a guarantee}

\label{lesson:HI-C557-garanti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a worry, then the Hindi for peace of mind, ease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{गारंटी}}
\textbf{\hi{गारंटी}} — \emph{gāraṇṭī} — \textquotedblleft{}a guarantee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दुकानदार} \hi{ने} \hi{घड़ी} \hi{पर} \hi{एक} \hi{साल} \hi{की} \hi{गारंटी} \hi{दी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dukāndār ne ghaṛī par ek sāl kī gāraṇṭī dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper gave a one-year guarantee on the watch.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{गारंटी}} (\emph{gāraṇṭī}) is a loan from English \emph{guarantee}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{दुर्भाग्य} (durbhāgya)}{दुर्भाग्य (durbhāgya)}]{\hi{दुर्भाग्य} (durbhāgya) — misfortune; bad luck}

\label{lesson:HI-C557-durbhagya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for peace of mind, ease, then the Hindi for a guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{दुर्भाग्य}}
\textbf{\hi{दुर्भाग्य}} — \emph{durbhāgya} — \textquotedblleft{}misfortune; bad luck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दुर्भाग्य} \hi{से} \hi{हमारी} \hi{ट्रेन} \hi{छूट} \hi{गई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Durbhāgya se hamārī ṭren chūṭ gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Unfortunately we missed our train.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{दुर्भाग्य}} (\emph{durbhāgya}) is a tatsama, taken whole from Sanskrit \emph{durbhāgya}, \textquotedblleft{}ill luck\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durbhāgya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Durbhāgya se hamārī ṭren chūṭ gaī.} — Unfortunately we missed our train.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for peace of mind, ease, then the Hindi for a guarantee, then say \emph{durbhāgya} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ख़ौफ़} (khauf)}{ख़ौफ़ (khauf)}]{\hi{ख़ौफ़} (khauf) — fear, dread}

\label{lesson:HI-C557-khauf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a guarantee, then the Hindi for misfortune.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ख़ौफ़}}
\textbf{\hi{ख़ौफ़}} — \emph{khauf} — \textquotedblleft{}fear, dread\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{रात} \hi{को} \hi{जंगल} \hi{में} \hi{हमें} \hi{ख़ौफ़} \hi{लगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rāt ko jaṅgal meṁ hamẽ khauf lagā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We felt afraid in the forest at night.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ख़ौफ़}} (\emph{khauf}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{khawf}, \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a guarantee, then the Hindi for misfortune, then say \emph{khauf} again
\end{itemize}
